text:
What I have, my friend, is a profound

desire to sleep!... You know? Sleep

is a state of divinity.

The one who sleeps is a god... What I have,

my friend, is a great desire to sleep.


Sleep is in life our only world,

for wakefulness immerses us

in the common illusion, in the ocean

of so-called “Reality.” Awake

we all see the same thing:

we see earth, water, air, fire,

ephemeral creatures... Asleep,

each person is in their world,

in their exclusive world:

hermetic, closed to alien eyes,

to alien souls; each mind spins

its own dream (or its truth: who knows?)


Not even the most adored being

can enter with us through the door

of our sleep. Not even the wife

who shares your bed

and hears you converse with the phantoms

that cross your spirit

while you sleep could,

even if she longed to,

cross the thresholds of that world,

your wondrous world of shadows.


O blessed are those who sleep!

For them each night the universe

that our spirit creates each day

is extinguished with all its pain.

When they put out its light, the cosmos goes out.


The greatest punishment is wakefulness:

insomnia is exile

from the best paradise...


No one, not even the happiest, would want

to subtract hours from sleep to be happy.

Not even the beloved woman

is worth a gentle, serene sleep

in the arms of Him who suggests

holy inspirations...

“The day belongs to men; but the night

belongs to the gods,” the ancients said.


Do not disturb my peace, then, with your speeches,

friend: you know much;

but my sleep knows more... Go away!

I want neither glory nor inheritance:

what I have, my friend, is a profound

desire to sleep...

translation.title: Sleep
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Nervo’s metaphysics of sleep as a private world and the final contrast between human day and divine night.
